channel.title: Kataban Blog
channel.description: A blog for overseas collectors hunting down Japanese retro games — shop guides, import how-tos, and the stories behind the titles.

item.title: Onimusha: Warlords — A Buying Guide to the PS2 Original
item.description: Onimusha: Warlords launched Capcom's samurai-action series on the PlayStation 2 in 2001. Here's the product code, what to check on a listing, and where to buy the Japanese original.

item.title: Shinyaku DoDonPachi Dai-Fukkatsu Just Launched — Here's Where the Series Came From
item.description: CAVE's bullet-hell classic got a new Steam release on August 27. Here are the four original Japanese releases the DoDonPachi series is built on, with product codes.

item.title: Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 2 Just Shipped Three Originals
item.description: Master Collection Vol. 2 landed August 27 with MGS4, Peace Walker, and Ghost Babel. Here's where to find the original Japanese releases of all three, with product codes.

item.title: Akihabara Deep Cuts: BEEP and the Retro Game Camp Dungeon
item.description: Two specialist Akihabara shops for retro PC hardware, arcade boards, and cartridge piles — BEEP Akihabara and the Retro Game Camp Dungeon Store, both a short walk beyond the routes in Parts 1 and 2.

item.title: Persona 4 Revival Gets a February 2027 Release Date and New Story Trailer
item.description: Persona 4 Revival launches February 18, 2027 on PS5, Xbox, and PC. Atlus revealed a new story trailer at Gamescom 2026 — find the games that started it all.

item.title: Capcom Announces "Mega Man: Dual Override" for the Series' 40th Anniversary
item.description: Capcom announced Mega Man: Dual Override for 2027, with both Mega Man and Proto Man playable. Here's what was revealed, and where the series started on the Famicom in 1987.

item.title: "Console Archives BUBBLE BOBBLE" Brings the 1987 Disk System Original to Switch 2 and PS5
item.description: HAMSTER's Console Archives series brings BUBBLE BOBBLE to Switch 2 and PS5. The 1987 Famicom original was a Disk System release, not a cartridge — here's what that means for collectors.

item.title: What Does "CIB" Mean When Buying Used Games in Japan?
item.description: CIB (Complete In Box) means the game, case, and manual are all present. Here's what to check before buying, and how it maps to Japanese listing terms.

item.title: Terranigma Is Getting a Remaster in 2027 — Here's the Original SFC Version
item.description: The 1995 Enix/Quintet classic Terranigma (Tenchi Souzou) is coming back in 2027 on modern platforms. Here's what was announced, and where to find the original Super Famicom release.

item.title: Ninja JaJaMaru-kun Is Back — A New Action Game Is Coming in 2027
item.description: City Connection has announced Jajamaru no Hyakki Yakouden, a new dungeon-crawling action game in the 40-year-old Ninja JaJaMaru-kun series. Here's what was revealed, and where to find the original 1985 Famicom game.

item.title: The Akihabara Chain-Store Crawl: Four Big Names, Four Very Different Shelves
item.description: Suruga-ya, Hard Off, Book-Off and Lashinbang all sell used games in Akihabara — but they stock, price and close at completely different hours. Here's which door to walk through.

item.title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 Is Coming — And the Japanese Alien Games That Came Before It
item.description: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 releases August 25, 2026. Here's what Japan's game database actually holds from the games that came before it — and why the closest thing you can buy isn't officially Aliens.

item.title: What Does "Junk" Mean When Buying Used Games in Japan?
item.description: In Japanese used game shops, "Junk" (ジャンク) doesn't mean broken — it means "sold as-is, no guarantee." Here's what that really means before you buy.

item.title: Golden Axe Is Getting an Anime. Here's What the Original Japanese Releases Actually Look Like
item.description: Paramount+ drops the Golden Axe anime on September 16. Here is what the five original Japanese releases actually are, which versions never left Japan, and the product codes to search them by.

item.title: Fire Emblem: Where It All Began — 5 Famicom & Super Famicom Games You Can Import Today
item.description: Before Awakening, before Three Houses — discover the five Famicom and Super Famicom games that started Fire Emblem, and how to import them from Japan.

item.title: Akihabara's Chuo-dori Retro Row: The Essential First Walk for Overseas Collectors
item.description: The core Akihabara retro game walk along Chuo-dori — four legendary shops, one straight line, no Japanese required.

item.title: How to Buy Japanese Retro Games Without Reading Japanese
item.description: A step-by-step guide to finding, identifying, and buying used Japanese retro games online — no Japanese literacy required.
